title: Worksheet 1: What Are Data Types?
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: In programming, every piece of data a computer works with has a specific "data type," which tells the computer what kind of information is being stored and what operations can be performed on it. Common basic data types include integers, which are whole numbers with no decimal point; floating-point numbers, often called "floats," which are numbers that include a decimal point; strings, which are sequences of text characters; and booleans, which can only hold one of two values, true or false. A computer treats each data type differently: for example, adding two integers together performs mathematical addition, but "adding" two strings together usually joins them end to end instead of performing any math. Understanding data types is important because using the wrong type in the wrong place, such as trying to perform math on a string that isn't actually a number, can cause a program to behave unexpectedly or crash entirely.

questions.text: According to the paragraph, what happens when two strings are "added" together?
questions.correct: They are usually joined end to end
